fact: Sierra Leone's regulator NatCA states that in November 2024 Guinea and Sierra Leone signed an agreement to interconnect their national internet backbone networks.

Guinea's backbone manager SOGEB and Sierra Leone's Leoncom signed an interconnection agreement in Conakry to link their national fibre networks at Pamelap on the border, with initial capacity of 42.5 Gbps and 100 Gbps planned by 2026; the document gives no event date, so its published date 2025-06-23 is used.
In June 2024 Guinea's SOGEB and Mali's SMTD agreed, with ministry facilitation, to interconnect the two countries' fibre networks.
Guinea's telecoms ministry says four operational cross-border interconnections with Mali, Senegal, Cote d'Ivoire and Sierra Leone were achieved in 2025.
The ROA-BN chairman said Mali is connected to Guinea within the operational eight-country backbone network, whose headquarters opened in Conakry on 10 November 2025.

Guinea's minister Rose Pola Pricemou and Sierra Leone's minister Salima Monorma Bah signed a framework agreement in Freetown on 22 November 2024 that includes interconnecting the two countries' national internet backbones, per Agence Ecofin.
Agence Ecofin reports that the Ivorian and Guinean ministers signed on 11 October 2024 a partnership agreement to interconnect the two countries' fibre optic networks.
WACREN, supported by European Commission co-funded AfricaConnect projects, says Guinea joins its research and education network backbone.

Minister Rose Pola Pricemou of Guinea and Cote d'Ivoire's minister Kalil Konate signed a protocol in Conakry on 11 October 2024 on interconnecting the two countries' fibre-optic networks, says the Ivorian government portal.

Sierra Leone's communications ministry reports that Guinea and Sierra Leone signed a framework agreement on 22 November 2024 covering infrastructure sharing and the linking of fibre networks, to be overseen by regulators ARPT and NaTCA and a joint commission.
